A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multilingual TruthfulQA study. Their complete texts, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including matching the reordered appendices D and E.

before.justification: v1 reports original human assessments, MC2 and judge evaluations, translation comparisons, and analyses of universal versus contextual questions.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds multilingual model-output examples in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The translation procedures, MC2 evaluation, and fine-tuned truthfulness and informativeness judges remain the same. Newly supplied training details do not establish a changed algorithm, architecture or training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 817-question benchmark across English, Spanish, Catalan, Galician and Basque, including professional and machine translations and universal/contextual subsets. Appendix F illustrates existing coverage without introducing another task or test scenario.

E2.justification: The same 12 evaluated models and the same judge candidates participate in the corresponding comparisons. The cross-family judge comparison already appears in v1 Appendix D and moves to v3 Appendix E without changing comparator membership.

E3.justification: The human-evaluation sample, binary annotation rules, six-shot MC2 procedure, metrics and 288/529-question partition are retained. The learning rate and epoch count first supplied in v3 document existing experiments rather than revise previously stated settings.

E4.justification: New Appendix F provides two multilingual Gemma 2 27B response examples, adding concrete case-study evidence about answer detail and cross-language differences. The existing informativeness, judge-family, translation and universal/contextual analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same Cohen kappa agreement reporting and chi-square comparison, including the reported p-value range of 0.18–0.78. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or another uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 2–8 and the existing charts are unchanged; for example, Gemma-2-27b-it retains Table 4 averages of 61.3 for MC2 and 79.0 for Judge-LLM. Appendix F adds previously unreported qualitative outputs for quote attribution and the tortoise-versus-hare question.

T1.justification: Neither version presents theoretical proofs or a formal theoretical contribution. No mathematical definition, assumption, theorem or derivation is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The multilingual benchmark contribution and headline conclusions about language differences, model size, judge agreement, informativeness, machine translation and contextual questions remain the same. The added examples support existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 corrects the reversed assertion about benchmarks lacking time- and context-independent questions: v3 instead says lacking dependent questions makes benchmarks quickly solvable, consistent with Figure 2. Section 5 also qualifies approximately 90% performance as applying to the best models. The substantive limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies a judge learning rate of 0.01 and five epochs, identifies native-speaking professional translators and authors as evaluators, and names the implementation used for translation metrics. It also expands the stated resource availability to include models and supplies a datasets/models collection link.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds Wang et al. (2024), Liu et al. (2025), Qi et al. (2023) and Lai et al. (2023) concerning cross-language factual consistency and multilingual instruction tuning. It also explains VeritasQA's question composition. These modestly expand the background without substantially redefining the contribution.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized language edits, clarifies descriptions and cross-references, standardizes model-name capitalization, and exchanges the order of appendices D and E. The main section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 6 containing boxed response examples, reorders Figure 5 and Table 8 within the appendices, adds alternating shading to Table 8, and adjusts table sizing, placement and captions. The existing charts themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency through training settings, evaluator and translator provenance, and expanded resource-access information. Appendix F makes the qualitative discussion more inspectable, while Section 4.1 corrects a contradictory interpretation. These are limited gains: quantitative evidence is unchanged, and the existing discrepancy between the prose's 8B judge and Table 8's 70B label remains unresolved.
